title: Foundation self-host canary
description: Objective: prove Foundation Preview on Windows with pinned Claude and one exclusive low-risk moe-next task. Deliverable: J1/J3/J4, hostile-client, crash, handoff, session-coordination, and self-host evidence under tests/e2e/foundation plus a release manifest. NOT in scope: fan-out, best-tool claims, old-Moe cutover, or benchmark confirmatory data. Hard dependencies: every preceding SH task and completion of the cleanup lane. Owned paths: tests/e2e/foundation/** and release evidence paths only. Verification: pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm test:e2e.
definitionOfDone: Fresh frozen-lockfile install and all Foundation typecheck, repository, fault, security, and E2E gates pass at one exact commit.
J1, J3, and J4 pass with bounded actions, crash recovery, stale-command fencing, rejection/replan, and safe handoff.
One exclusive task completes plan, execute, verify, independent review, accept, and typed session/terminal communication with exact receipts and no duplicate authority.
Old Moe records the canary as externally delegated so no second worker owns it; no unresolved authority UNKNOWN or foreign-path admission remains.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: Build the harness foundation — buildable today, independent of every in-flight feature. Create tests/e2e/foundation/foundation-fixtures.ts providing the INPUTS a journey needs: a scratch project repository, a seeded low-risk task definition, and a pinned Claude runtime observation. Fixtures supply inputs only — they may NEVER stand in for a component under certification, because mocking the system under test would make this suite an elaborate tautology. Create tests/e2e/foundation/e2e-harness.ts with the run scaffolding: deterministic seeds as fixed literals (no Math.random, no wall clock, so a failing journey is reproducible), a declared-boundary process control used ONLY by this harness and never imported into a package, and cleanup that runs on every exit path including failure — on Windows a killed child holds handles and a leaked fixture directory will fail later cases with EBUSY rather than with the real error.

SPLIT DECLARED: the step named two modules; I landed three. Declared-boundary process control is in its own e2e-process.ts rather than inside e2e-harness.ts. Reason is the step's own containment requirement — the kill capability is the one thing that must never reach a package, and a separate module makes the containment scannable and keeps both files far under the cap. Same owned directory, no new dependency.

WHAT THE HARNESS GUARANTEES, each asserted not promised:
- Determinism. E2E_SEED is frozen fixed literals (runPrefix, logicalEpochUtc 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, logicalStepMs 1000). createLogicalClock() is a pure counter formatted by arithmetic — it constructs no Date at all — and a fresh clock always restarts at the epoch. deterministicId(kind, ordinal) is pure. A test scans the RAW text of all three harness modules for Math.random / Date.now / new Date( / performance.now and requires zero hits. It caught my own doc comment on the first run, which is how I know the scan is live; I reworded the prose rather than switching to comment-stripping, because a raw-text scan cannot be fooled by a parser edge case and the stricter check is the right one to keep.
- Cleanup on EVERY exit path. finishE2eRun runs entries LIFO, never stops early, and returns the stable code E2E_CLEANUP_FAILED with the failing labels. withE2eRun cleans up in `finally` and rethrows the body error unchanged; a cleanup failure on an otherwise-successful body is raised, because a canary that leaked a process is not a passing canary. Scratch removal uses rm maxRetries:10 retryDelay:100, and the process cleanup awaits the child's actual exit before the directory is removed — on Windows the handle outlives the kill and the EBUSY would surface in the NEXT case instead of this one.
- Declared boundaries. DECLARED_BOUNDARIES is frozen and non-empty; a kill outside it is refused E2E_UNDECLARED_BOUNDARY and the process verifiably stays alive (handle.killedAt stays null). A second kill of the same handle is refused E2E_PROCESS_ALREADY_KILLED, which matters because a J3 case that killed one handle twice would look like two crash boundaries while being one. An unknown target throws E2E_UNKNOWN_KILL_TARGET BEFORE spawning, so no orphan exists that no cleanup entry owns. KILL_TARGETS is set-equality-asserted against the design's three: agent, daemon, runner. NOTE the design does not enumerate the boundaries themselves, so that list is ours — declared and frozen, which is what makes "at declared boundaries" falsifiable.
- Containment. A test walks packages/, apps/ and adapters/ and requires zero references to e2e-harness or tests/e2e/foundation, and asserts the walk visited >100 files first, so an empty scan cannot fake the pass (epic rail 6).

FIXTURES SUPPLY INPUTS ONLY. No test double of any certified component exists in this directory. The one production import is on the input side and is deliberate: pinnedClaudeRuntimeObservation() calls the REAL buildProviderRuntimeObservation from packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-observation.ts with the harness's fixed clock, so the fixture cannot drift from the shape production emits and a contract change surfaces as a thrown refusal carrying its own code, never as a swallowed default. Verified it lands truthClass PROVEN, pinningMethod CONTENT_ADDRESSED_COPY, and the same observationDigest on two builds. A hand-rolled literal here would have been the "test helper reimplements the production surface" defect epic rail 6 names.

implementationPlan.description: Build the release manifest and the exact-commit gate — DoD 1, and also buildable today. Create tests/e2e/foundation/release-manifest.ts and release-manifest.test.ts. The manifest binds, for one canary run: the exact commit SHA, the frozen-lockfile install result, every gate that ran with its outcome, and the digests of the evidence each journey produced. Assert the two properties that make it meaningful rather than decorative: the working tree was CLEAN at the start of the run and every gate ran at the SAME commit — a canary assembled from a dirty tree, or whose gates were run at different commits, proves nothing about a release. Use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` as part of the claim, not as a convenience, and record its result in the manifest. The manifest is immutable and content-addressed; assert its digest covers every field by set equality against a hand-written list.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD, RED verified for the right reason: release-manifest.test.ts written first, first run failed with `Cannot find module './journey-spec.js'` — a real missing-module red, not a no-tests-collected red. Then implemented to green.

GREEN, foreground, repo root: `npx vitest run --root . tests/e2e/foundation` -> 2 files, 32 passed, 0 failed. `npx tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json` -> exit 0.

FILES: release-manifest.ts 217, release-manifest.test.ts 240, journey-spec.ts 189. All under the 250 target.

THE TWO PROPERTIES THAT MAKE THE MANIFEST A CLAIM, both implemented as REFUSALS so no partially authoritative object escapes: treeCleanAtStart !== true -> RELEASE_MANIFEST_DIRTY_TREE; any gate whose commitSha differs from the manifest commit -> RELEASE_MANIFEST_COMMIT_MISMATCH. Six more codes complete the fail-closed surface: COMMIT_INVALID, INSTALL_NOT_FROZEN, INSTALL_FAILED, GATE_RED, GATE_EMPTY, EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE. The code list is frozen, duplicate-free, and asserted by set equality against a hand-written literal.

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` IS PART OF THE CLAIM, NOT A CONVENIENCE: FROZEN_LOCKFILE_COMMAND is compared exactly, so a manifest built from a plain `pnpm install` is refused INSTALL_NOT_FROZEN and a non-zero install is refused INSTALL_FAILED. "We installed from the lockfile" cannot be asserted by a run that did not.

DIGEST COVERS EVERY FIELD, asserted two independent ways because the name check alone is weak:
1. Set equality of `Object.keys(releaseManifestDigestInput(manifest))` against a HAND-WRITTEN literal in the test file. Deliberately not imported from the module under test — a list the module exports could not detect a field the module silently dropped.
2. Behavioural: perturbing each field that CAN vary changes the digest. Honest limitation stated in the test: only commitSha, gates and journeyEvidence can vary inside an accepted manifest, because treeCleanAtStart must be true and install must be the frozen command at exit 0 or the build refuses. Those two are pinned by their refusal codes instead, which is stronger than a digest delta. The commitSha perturbation moves the gates with it, since a manifest whose gates ran elsewhere is refused — noted in a comment so a reader does not mistake it for a two-field test.
Digest provably does not cover itself: asserted that `manifestDigest` is absent from the digest input keys. Manifest is deepFrozen and reproducible (same input -> same digest).

REUSED PRODUCTION SURFACES rather than reimplementing: canonicalDigest, isCommitIdentity, isHex64, deepFreeze from packages/runner/src/canonical.ts. A hashing or validation helper rewritten in test code is the detached-assertion defect epic rail 6 names.

journey-spec.ts LANDED HERE as promised in step 3, and it now has a real consumer: the manifest's evidence completeness is checked against FOUNDATION_EXIT_SET, so a canary missing a journey's evidence is refused EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE. It carries the step-1 hand transcription with verbatim design quotes and line anchors (J1 1095, J3 1099, J4 1101, rejection routing 1087, release-handoff 337, exit 1324) so a reviewer can diff the quotes against the design without trusting the file. It records explicitly that the design does NOT enumerate hostile-client cases and that J2/J5/J6 are deliberately absent from Foundation Preview (Phase 5/6, design lines 1097/1103/1105/1330/1336) — adding one would widen the cutover gate beyond what the design requires.

implementationPlan.description: J1 — the linear Tuesday-bug journey, against the REAL daemon command surface and the REAL store. Create tests/e2e/foundation/j1-linear-task.e2e.test.ts asserting the design's own claim at line 1095: after bootstrap, one causal bug remains one worker node, and the per-goal happy-path human actions are EXACTLY three — goal.create, exact plan/initial-graph approval, and final acceptance of the verified and reviewed result. Assert that count exactly: a journey needing a fourth human action has failed the design's claim, and a journey needing fewer has skipped an approval gate. Assert the run produces exact diffs and receipts, and that control-plane overhead is reported. Drive it end to end through the daemon's command path — no mock of any component under certification. If a required command surface is absent, this test FAILS or the task blocks; it is never stubbed.

J3 — crash recovery, design line 1099. Create tests/e2e/foundation/j3-crash-recovery.e2e.test.ts killing the agent, the runner and the daemon at DECLARED boundaries (this harness is the only place in the epic where real process termination is legitimate; the runner subtree is deliberately fenced against it). After each restart assert that the system shows the honest record — adopted, suspect, quarantined, and reconciliation records with their truth chips — rather than a silently resumed run. Assert the two properties that distinguish honest recovery from a cover-up: healthy continuation is ONE safe action or an already-approved policy action, and it creates a traceable continuation or binding record and NEVER edits history — compare the pre-crash records byte-for-byte after recovery to prove nothing was rewritten. Assert the outcome kinds by set equality against the hand-written list from step 1, so an unexpected recovery outcome fails rather than passing unnoticed.

J4 — rejection and re-plan, design line 1101. Create tests/e2e/foundation/j4-rejection-replan.e2e.test.ts asserting: findings link evidence to required changes (a finding with no evidence link fails); delta approval shows changed hashes and correctly classifies invalidated versus carry-forward nodes; the three-round counter is VISIBLE and escalation is EXPLICIT, tested at the boundary — two rounds do not escalate, the third does; and old plans, attempts, receipts and reviews remain READABLE after a re-plan, which is the immutability half and the one most easily lost, so assert the earlier records are still retrievable and byte-identical rather than merely that a new plan exists.

Hostile-client and release-handoff incident fixtures — named in the design's exit condition at line 1324 and in this task's deliverable. Create tests/e2e/foundation/hostile-client.e2e.test.ts driving the adapter boundary with deliberately hostile input: oversized bodies, malformed envelopes, replayed commands, stale cursors, forged or absent authentication, and free-form session/terminal text attempting to trigger a state change. Assert each is refused with its stable code at the boundary and that NONE produces a durable mutation — read the store back to prove the non-mutation rather than trusting the response, since a service that mutates and then refuses would pass a response-only assertion. Include the release-handoff incident: an attempt released mid-flight must leave an exact safe handoff and no partial authority. Assert the case list length is non-zero so a hostile sweep that generates nothing cannot pass.

Prove the self-host claim — DoD 3, the point of the whole canary. Assert that ONE exclusive low-risk moe-next task completes the full arc through the real system: plan, execute, verify, independent review, accept, with typed session and terminal communication throughout, producing exact receipts and NO duplicate authority. The duplicate-authority assertion is the load-bearing one — assert that at no point do two workers hold authority over the same task, checked across the whole run rather than at the end, since a transient overlap that resolves before completion is exactly the bug this gate exists to catch. Assert every session and terminal message is advisory and that none of them caused a state change except through the command path. Record the receipts in the release manifest from step 4.

Run the full gate at ONE exact commit and assemble the evidence. From a clean tree at a recorded commit SHA: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm test:e2e`, capturing real output for each. All must exit 0 at the SAME commit — gates run at different commits do not compose into a release claim, and that is what DoD 1 is asserting. Record the commit SHA, the install result, and each gate's outcome in the release manifest. Attribute any red by path and never by a remembered count. Then DoD 4's external half: 'Old Moe records the canary as externally delegated so no second worker owns it' is a real coordination action against another system, NOT a test assertion — do not perform it as a side effect of a passing run. Ask for explicit human confirmation before performing it, and record the confirmation. Finally confirm no unresolved authority UNKNOWN and no foreign-path admission remains, asserted rather than eyeballed.

Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec. Read the suite as an attacker: is any component under certification mocked or stubbed anywhere — the tautology failure that would make this whole gate worthless; was any journey assertion weakened, skipped, or narrowed so it would pass against a partial system; were the journey expectations transcribed by hand from the design or quietly derived from the implementation; does J3 actually kill real processes at declared boundaries, and does it prove history was not rewritten rather than merely that recovery happened; does the hostile suite read the store back to prove non-mutation; can two workers ever hold authority over the same task at any instant during the run; did every gate genuinely run at one commit from a clean tree; does any harness process leak on a failure path. Then stage and commit by EXPLICIT PER-FILE pathspec — never a bare git commit, never git commit -a, never git add -A, never a directory — since the working tree is shared with many in-flight tasks. Root package.json is committed only if step 2's amendment was granted. Run `git status --porcelain` first, unstage foreign paths with `git restore --staged`, and verify with `git show --stat` that only owned paths landed with no probe, scratch or debug files.

planningNotes.risks:
1. **THE CANARY MUST NOT BE WEAKENED TO PASS.** This is the cutover acceptance gate for the epic. If a journey cannot run because a feature is absent, the journey FAILS or the task blocks — it is never narrowed, stubbed, or asserted against a mock of the thing under test. A green canary over a partial system is the single worst outcome available here, worse than no canary, because it certifies a cutover that did not happen.
2. **Do not mock the system under test.** E2E means the real daemon command surface and the real store. Mocking a daemon service to make J1 pass would make this suite an elaborate tautology. Fixtures may supply INPUTS (a repo, a task, a pinned Claude runtime observation); they may never stand in for the components being certified.
3. **DoD 1 requires ONE EXACT COMMIT.** A canary assembled from a dirty tree, or whose gates were run at different commits, proves nothing about a release. Record the commit SHA and assert the tree is clean at the start of the run; a fresh frozen-lockfile install (`--frozen-lockfile`) is part of the claim, not a convenience.
4. **DoD 4 has an external, irreversible-feeling side**: 'Old Moe records the canary as externally delegated so no second worker owns it.' That is a real coordination action against another system, not a test assertion. Treat it as requiring explicit human confirmation before it is performed, and never perform it as a side effect of a passing test run.
5. **J3 kills processes at declared boundaries** — the only place in this epic where real process termination is legitimate, since the runner subtree is fenced against it. Confine that capability to the E2E harness, never import it into a package, and assert cleanup on every exit path so a killed child cannot leak into later cases (Windows holds handles; see the EBUSY temp-fixture memory).
6. **Do not derive the expected journey assertions from the implementation.** Transcribe them by hand from design lines 1095/1099/1101 (`mem:gotcha-self-derived-universe-cannot-check-itself`), or the canary asserts only that the system does what it does.
7. Root `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are shared with every in-flight task — single-hunk change, verified with `git diff --stat`, committed by explicit pathspec.
8. `pnpm test` at root currently includes other packages' suites; do not let this task's lane silently change what that script covers.
